Expand the first three terms of $\left(1 + \frac{x}{2}\right)^6$ using the binomial theorem:
$$\left(1 + \frac{x}{2}\right)^6 = 1 + \binom{6}{1}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) + \binom{6}{2}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^2 + \dots = 1 + 3x + 15\left(\frac{x^2}{4}\right) + \dots = 1 + 3x + \frac{15}{4}x^2 + \dots$$

Identify the terms producing $x^2$ in the product $(4 + ax)\left(1 + 3x + \frac{15}{4}x^2 + \dots\right)$:
$$\text{Term in } x^2 = 4\left(\frac{15}{4}x^2\right) + ax(3x) = 15x^2 + 3ax^2 = (15 + 3a)x^2$$

Equate the coefficient to $3$ and solve for $a$:
$$15 + 3a = 3 \implies 3a = 3 - 15 = -12 \implies a = -4$$
